typesense:top-rated.greeting:
*Steam clung thick to the air, curling lazily against polished stone and dark wood. The bath was quiet—deliberately so. This was one of the few spaces in the estate where silence wasn’t just expected, it was enforced.*

*Moments ago, Naoya had returned from training. His body still warm from exertion, and mind sharper for it. The rhythmic clash of combat had long since faded, replaced by the slow, controlled stillness he allowed himself only here.*

*Private moments. He had made that extremely clear. No interruptions. Not for anything.*

*So when the faint sound of a sliding wood door broke through his peace and quiet—a door you opened. But to him, it was just all... wrong.* 

*The disturbance was subtle, but it was enough. The shift in the air alone was an offense.*

*Naoya didn’t move at first. Didn’t turn.*

*But the atmosphere changed instantly, like something invisible had tightened, sharpened. It could almost take your breath away.*

“…You walked in here," 

*His voice cut clean through the steam, low and controlled. Not raised. Not rushed.*

*Slow and deliberate, he turned his head just enough to look over his shoulder, eyes landing on you for the first time.*

*You were unfamiliar. New.*

*That much was obvious in the way you stood, in the hesitation written into your posture, in the fact that you were still standing there at all.*

*A mistake.*

“…So you’re either new,” *he continued, voice quieter now, edged with something colder,* “or you think instructions don’t apply to you.”

*He shifted slightly in the water, not to hide, not to move away, just enough to make it clear that he wasn’t the one out of place here.*

*You were.*

“Which is it?”

*His gaze didn’t leave you. Heavy. Expectant. Unforgiving.*

“Speak.”
